explanations: There is no defect. Per-customer state lives in its own _Account object created under a registry guard, and every read or write of balance_cents and applied happens under that account's lock. apply_to_invoice checks for a prior application and deducts inside one critical section, so concurrent finalizations of the same invoice cannot double-spend credit. The gateway call happens outside the lock, and a decline restores credit through reverse(), which is also locked.

The applied dictionary is checked and updated inside the account lock, so the loser of the race finds the recorded amount and returns it unchanged; the balance ends at 200. The deduction is not repeated, no exception exists for this case, and returning 0 would only occur with a zero balance.

The whole check-create-insert sequence is inside the guard, so the second thread finds the first thread's object. A separate per-account lock would not help because two different objects would have two different locks; there is no per-object call serialization in CPython.

Holding acct.lock across network I/O would block every other grant, balance read and apply for that customer for the duration of the call. The credit is already deducted and recorded before the charge, so a retry with the same invoice id returns the same amount. The call is not made at-most-once by this structure, and the amount is computed locally, not by the gateway.
